description_full: Gladstone Land Corporation is a publicly traded real estate investment trust that invests in farmland located in major agricultural markets in the U.S., which it leases to farmers. The Company currently owns 143 farms, comprised of approximately 98,000 acres in 14 different states and nearly 56,000 acre-feet of water assets in California. Gladstone Land Corporation was established in 1997 and was incorporated in Maryland.

financial_summary: Gladstone Land Corporation is a micro-cap real estate business with a $298M market cap on $88M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -0% over the past three years and +22% annually across the full decade — essentially flat, and a business treading water is rarely a path to compounding.
Returns on capital run at 2% against a 6% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 12.9× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 1.2× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.
Management returns a meaningful 6.9% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 5.9% of the shares.
